requirements.summary: Needle 3 performs real Windows/Node planning and extraction using a pinned WASM or executable artifact, without consumer pip/compile requirements.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). The pinned-artifact half is real: the Windows x86_64 needle.exe and needle3.cact are pinned by HF revision with digests verified through the host's acquisition path (NDL-01, round 48), and the extension's provider performs one-shot planning/extraction through the managed process bridge with the listener refused and no pip/compile anywhere. The engine WAS executed on this host with a real tool call recorded (2026-10-14). Remaining: no fresh Windows/Node planning run has been re-executed against the artifacts on this machine in the acceptance-suite sense (the real-engine tests skip without env-provided copies), and no second differing revision has been observed to prove the pin refuses one.

requirements.summary: A multi-intent Needle request returns validated proposals; instrumented target tools prove zero actual execution until a separate approved dispatch. Off-topic/no-match behavior is tested.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Multi-intent proposal validation, instrumented-target zero-execution proof, and off-topic/no-match behavior need the planning adapter wired into the host registry; the adapter is the MODEL-03 blocked remainder. The extension's provider validates single proposals, but no multi-intent suite exists.

requirements.summary: Needle receives only the authorized frozen schema subset; malicious names, arguments, unavailable tools and returned management/self-recursive calls are rejected.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). The authorized-frozen-schema-subset and malicious-name/argument rejection halves need the planning contract registered with a real schema intersection; no Needle tool is registered, so there is no surface to attack or defend.

requirements.summary: Extraction schema bounds and unsupported grammar constraints are checked; valid JSON with wrong field facts fails the separate quality tests instead of being called correct.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Extraction schema bounds and grammar-constraint checks are the adapter slice (MODEL-03 blocked); the extension's own extraction contract exists but is not exercised against a live planning/extraction flow.

requirements.summary: Needle requests do not retain another caller's prompt/state; native cancellation, overflow and supported telemetry opt-out are checked with process/network observation.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Cross-caller prompt/state isolation is structural (process-per-call, no session id, no conversation buffer) but no multi-caller observation test exists; native cancellation/overflow/telemetry-opt-out checks need instrumented live runs that do not exist.

requirements.summary: Built-in `describe_image` is an ordinary declarative extension tool callable through DSH Native, MCP and hosted Code Mode, not special host prompt code.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). describe_image IS an ordinary recipe tool, not host prompt code: it is built from a frozen recipe through the shared broker (RCP-12's 'the built-ins are two recipes through one broker, not two code paths' test), its input schema comes from the recipe, it calls no other tool, and the HLM-11/HLM-12 suite tests the real media-refusal behavior (text-only provider refused without being called, non-image modality refused at the binding). Remaining: callable through DSH Native/MCP/hosted Code Mode is not demonstrated end to end — the tool is built and unit-tested, but not registered and driven through all three surfaces.

requirements.summary: A recording fake provider proves real image content/reference reaches the image request path; passing only filename/FileBlock/text placeholder fails the test.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60, corrected round 62). The recording-fake-provider half is real: 'describes an image that reached the provider as typed media' proves real typed content reaches the request path, and a path-or-URL image is REFUSED rather than bound (recipes.test.ts 'refuses an image that is a path rather than typed media' — a filename alone cannot pass), plus the text-only provider is refused before invocation. Remaining: FileBlock/text-placeholder inputs through the BUILT-IN's invoke are not driven (the placeholder refusals are at the binding layer), and no test asserts a placeholder-shaped fake-provider record is rejected.

requirements.summary: Text-only, unknown-capability, inaccessible/offloaded image and unsupported MIME routes fail before a provider request; no silent vision fallback.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60, corrected round 62). The refusal routes exist and are tested at the recipe layer: text-only providers are refused without being called, unknown-capability providers are refused, a non-image media type (image/gif) is refused at the binding, and no silent vision fallback exists (nothing to fall back to). Remaining: the honesty clause names unclear/cropped/unreadable detail, not inaccessible/offloaded-image routes (corrected), and the built-in describe_image drives only an application/pdf refusal while the other unsupported-MIME cases live at the binding layer.

requirements.summary: Native caller-model selection captures the actual calling agent's model generation, not the last global model; concurrent model changes cannot alter an in-flight call's destination.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Native caller-model selection is untested: no mechanism captures the calling agent's model generation per call, and no concurrent-model-change scenario exists to alter an in-flight call's destination. The invocation context carries identity but not a caller-model field.

requirements.summary: MCP harness execution requires its explicit approved profile. No-profile and cross-client profile access fail without using UI conversation/credentials.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). MCP harness execution with an explicit approved profile: the capture-path module defines the profile vocabulary and the broker refuses to construct without a journal sink, but no MCP-side harness execution profile exists to approve, and the no-profile/cross-client refusals are therefore untestable.

requirements.summary: Auxiliary requests contain only recipe instructions and supplied bindings, no parent history/system prompt/tools/skills/secrets; side-call results do not mutate the parent dialogue.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60, upgraded round 62 per review). The wire-shape isolation IS asserted: the broker request carries EXACTLY {maxOutputTokens, prompt, signal} with no tools, no history and no system prompt on the wire (broker.test.ts:107,116-131), so a parent's conversation cannot ride along structurally. Remaining: no adversarial test feeds parent history/secrets through a composition and asserts they never reach the provider, and side-call results not mutating the parent dialogue is the broker contract, untested end to end.

requirements.summary: A model-emitted tool call fails; no nested agent loop or recursive image/composition/management call runs.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). The failing-tool-call path is real: the broker surfaces an UNEXPECTED_MODEL_TOOL_CALL for a stray tool call (broker.test.ts), and there is no nested-agent-loop or recursive-call code anywhere to run one (structural absence). Remaining: no test drives a model-emitted failing call through the full tool surface and asserts the absence of a retry loop.

requirements.summary: Refusal, truncation, invalid JSON, missing terminal result, timeout and cancellation remain distinct; approved repair counts against the original attempt/token/deadline budget.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). The distinctions are enforced at the recipe layer: refusal, truncation and empty completion each produce a DISTINCT error with no title field (TOOL-06 suite), invalid JSON is surfaced as INVALID_MODEL_OUTPUT (RCP-04), and the run pipeline classifies cancellation separately from failure (RES-06). Repair counting against the original budget: repairs are COUNTED and the exhausted budget is reported as exhausted (TOOL-06), but the repair-budget-against-token/deadline-budget accounting is not implemented. Remaining: timeout distinctness at the recipe layer and the cross-budget accounting.

requirements.summary: Actual usage and model/location appear in bounded receipts; unknown usage is not zero cost. Remote vision/data-transfer grants are checked before upload.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Usage/model/location receipts exist for tool invocations (EXT-35) but no harness-execution receipt records actual usage, and 'unknown usage is not zero cost' has no accounting. Remote vision/data-transfer grant checks before upload: no upload path exists to check.

requirements.summary: Two independently configured live DSH vision routes can execute the same unchanged recipe; evidence identifies adapters/models and compares known image facts. Missing live access remains BLOCKED.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Two independently configured live DSH vision routes require two live vision providers; none exists in this build. The evidence-identity requirements (adapters/models named, known image facts compared) are moot without a route. The item's own clause — missing live access remains BLOCKED — applies in full.

requirements.summary: A new external author uses the CLI/template to create a typed harness recipe with schemas/skill/tests, pack it and install it without DSH/host source or custom inference code.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). No author CLI/template exists for creating a typed harness recipe with schemas/skill/tests; recipes are written as JSON in this repository. Packing and installing without DSH/host source is unproven for a fresh author.

requirements.summary: Recipe npm/HTTPS/local archive paths all remain install-inactive; activation publishes identical tools to DSH/MCP/Code Mode. Disable/deactivate/update/uninstall obey TMX and preserve unrelated packages.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). Recipe install paths (npm/HTTPS/local archive) are not implemented — the recipe packages ship in-repo; activation-publishes-identical-tools across DSH/MCP/Code Mode is untested; TMX-obedient disable/deactivate/update/uninstall for recipes is the extension lifecycle (tested for extensions, never for recipes).

requirements.summary: Malicious executable templates, unbound pointers, hidden prompt/network code, undeclared profiles, schema violations and recipe-generation identity changes fail validation/approval.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60, corrected round 62). Hostile-input VALIDATION exists at the recipe level — parseRecipe refuses executable template syntax, unbound pointers, unknown keys and prototype abuse (recipes.test.ts), and harness-serving validates at resolve time — but the requirement is about the INSTALL/APPROVAL surface: no hostile-recipe test suite drives a malicious template, hidden prompt/network code, undeclared profile, schema violation or identity change through package install and approval, because no recipe install/approval flow exists (AT-74's gap). NOT_RUN stands: the validation surface exists, the install surface it must protect does not.

requirements.summary: `text_title` uses the same generic recipe interpreter; no tool-name special case exists. Mixed semantic-rank→describe-image and STT→decision→title programs execute with accurate subcall accounting.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 60). The no-special-case half is tested: 'has no tool-name special case in the broker (RCP-12)' pins that text_title and describe_image flow through the SAME generic recipe interpreter, and the built-ins run against one broker instance with one policy. The title rules themselves are the TOOL-06 suite (refusals, invented-fact rejection, repair counting). Remaining: the mixed semantic-rank→describe-image and STT→decision→title programs cannot run — they need the embedding, STT and decision tools, none of which execute — so subcall accounting across such compositions is untested.

requirements.summary: A modern `tools/list`/`tools/call` succeeds as the first request without initialize/session; `server/discover` accurately reports the supported revision/features.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58, tightened round 59). First-request-without-handshake is the server's core property and is tested at three levels: the unit server answers tools/list AND tools/call as the FIRST request with no initialize and no session and retains nothing between dispatches (mcp-server.test.ts), the LIVE suite drives it over a real socket, and the fixture corpus captures tools/list and server/discover labeled as first application requests (the tools/call fixture records a successful call rather than carrying the first-request label — the call-as-first-request property is unit-proven). server/discover carries the fields the pinned schema REQUIRES and advertises only capabilities the server implements; the negative half — initialize at the old revision answered -32601 — is asserted live. Remaining: 'accurately reports the supported revision' is asserted as exactly-2026-07-28 in the unit suite and live; no independent third-party client has re-run against this host since the v2 packages left node_modules.

requirements.summary: Each request independently validates required metadata and unsupported versions/capabilities; a previous valid call does not authorize malformed following requests.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). Per-request independence is enforced and tested: metadata is parsed fresh per request and never from a previous one ('parses metadata fresh per request and never from a previous one', mcp-protocol.test.ts), a missing protocolVersion is rejected rather than defaulted, clientCapabilities is required while clientInfo is admitted-optional, a malformed clientInfo is rejected, an unsupported version carries -32022 with supported+requested, an unsupported REQUIRED capability is -32021, and no custom error occupies the reserved range. A previous valid call authorizing a malformed following request is the same no-retention property the 'retains nothing between two dispatches' test pins. Remaining: the sequence 'valid call then malformed call' is not driven as one ordered scenario over a live socket.

requirements.summary: Required HTTP headers/body fields and Base64 sentinel names are matched correctly; missing/mismatch/injection cases return the specified error before inference.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58, citation tightened round 59). Header/body/sentinel matching is tested: the MCP-Protocol-Version header must agree with the body (a mismatch is -32020 with HTTP 400), a named call must carry Mcp-Name and a matching one is accepted, the Base64-sentinel method header decodes correctly with the ACCEPT case tested at the HTTP layer (mcp-http.test.ts) and the wrong-decode/mismatch refusals at the protocol layer (mcp-protocol.test.ts), a request missing required metadata is invalid params with HTTP 400, and all of these fail BEFORE inference — the auth/header/parse layers precede dispatch in the request pipeline. Remaining: injection cases beyond the sentinel (a header that decodes to a DIFFERENT method than the body's) are refused at the header-check layer, but no dedicated injection test names the attack class explicitly.

requirements.summary: Every modern result has the correct resultType, valid structured content/output schema and final authorized canonical value; JSON-RPC errors and tool failures remain distinct.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). The result envelope is enforced: every result carries resultType and serverInfo metadata, an application failure is a tool-error RESULT not a JSON-RPC error, a malformed protocol request IS a JSON-RPC error, tool-error messages are bounded to stay model-readable, a successful call carries structuredContent with only the reserved meta removed and a bounded text rendering, and the LIVE suite Ajv-validates every response shape against the pinned schema including the tool-error and each error definition. Remaining: 'final authorized canonical value' is enforced at the host dispatch (the output schema check) and the MCP layer, but no single test asserts the canonical-value chain from the tool through structuredContent to the caller in one assertion.

requirements.summary: `subscriptions/listen` acknowledges first, filters requested authorized events and attaches the right subscription ID; interleaved callers/subscriptions do not leak catalog state.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). The subscription protocol is implemented and heavily tested: listen is accepted-as-required only when a registry is composed; the acknowledgement arrives as the RESULT and as a follow-up message with no event before it; unsupported requested filters are DROPPED rather than acknowledged; unrequested types are never acknowledged; the declared filters are exactly the served ones; events carry the subscription id and reach ONLY their subscriber; and one client's catalog change is NEVER delivered to another. Remaining: interleaved callers/subscriptions over a live socket are tested at the unit protocol level, not as a multi-client live scenario.

requirements.summary: HTTP stream closure and stdio cancellation abort only the corresponding request, including nested model work. The bridge stays alive for other calls.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). Request-scoped cancellation is enforced on both transports: the stdio bridge aborts EXACTLY the referenced request (per-request cancellation tests), reports a cancellation for a request it does not own, removes settled requests from the in-flight set, and EOF aborts ONLY bridge-owned requests while the bridge stays alive for others (mcp-stdio.test.ts); the HTTP side is per-request stateless so closure of one request cannot affect another; nested model work is cancelled through the caller signal propagation (the composition abort test aborts a running program). Remaining: HTTP stream-closure mid-request against nested model work is not driven end to end over a live socket.

requirements.summary: No legacy GET stream, protocol session dependency, standalone server RPC, Last-Event-ID replay, or falsely advertised optional sampling/tasks path is used by the modern implementation.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). The prohibitions hold structurally: the endpoint accepts POST only (GET is answered 405 with Allow: POST), there is no session concept anywhere in the dispatch layer ('retains nothing between two dispatches'), no standalone server RPC surface exists (the server is embedded, started by the host lifecycle), no Last-Event-ID or replay concept exists (grep: zero matches), and the subscriptions surface declares exactly the filters it serves with no falsely advertised sampling/tasks path (unsupported filters are dropped rather than acknowledged). Remaining: the prohibitions are asserted per-mechanism; no negative test drives each legacy shape at the wire and asserts its absence in one sweep.

requirements.summary: JSON Schema 2020-12, offline refs, bounded dynamic schema validation and private catalog-cache behavior pass independent fixtures.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). JSON Schema 2020-12 with offline refs is pinned: the schema records the exact source commit, is self-contained with no remote $ref (tested), defines every message this server sends, and both the fixture probe and the LIVE schema suite validate real responses against it — including each error's own definition, the 413 oversized-body shape, and the 202 notification acknowledgement. Bounded dynamic schema validation is the projected-output-schema work (never stricter than the contract, unsupported constraints rejected rather than silently dropped). Remaining: private catalog-cache behavior — the pinned schema's tools/list caching fields are carried (tested), but no independent fixture exercises a private catalog cache end to end.

requirements.summary: OAuth resource-server metadata, challenges, audience/scopes, token expiry/revocation and protected bridge credentials are tested; a custom static-token profile is not counted as OAuth conformance.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58, tightened round 59). The OAuth profile is tested across its surface: RFC 8414/9728 discovery metadata published, RFC 6750 challenges with the error code and scope named, audience/issuer/signature/expiry/unknown-client all refused, a not-yet-valid credential refused via its iat check (the future-dated half of nbf; no literal nbf field is read), per-client revocation with a peer left working, and — after the round-54 F4 fix — the §3.1 statuses (invalid_request 400, invalid_token 401, insufficient_scope 403). The static-token profile claims NO OAuth conformance (claimsOAuthConformance false, tested). Remaining: 'protected bridge credentials' — the bridge forwards the bearer credential but has no dedicated credential-protection test, and a custom static-token profile is not counted as OAuth (true by test), but no matrix test enumerates every profile's conformance claim.

requirements.summary: A modern SDK client and independent raw/schema probe test the packed server, with sanitized wire traces. Legacy compatibility tests, if offered, are separately labeled.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58, tightened round 59). The packed-server testing exists: verify:packed installs the real tarballs and probes the plugin by package name (PACKED-OK ×3), and the live MCP suites run the server mounted from source over real sockets (the BUILT host is exercised by verify:built and the packed proof, not by the MCP suites — corrected round 59). The modern SDK client half is the v2-interop suite — recorded at capture time as 6 tests 0 skipped in the fixture MANIFEST, currently SKIPPED here because the v2 packages are not installed (environment absence, corrected round 57). Sanitized wire traces: the fixture corpus (17 fixtures, 39 checks) captures messages with a credential placeholder, never a real token. Legacy compatibility tests: none exist, so nothing needs separate labeling. Remaining: no packed-server run drives the raw/schema probe AND the v2 client against the PACKED tarball in one scenario on this host.

requirements.summary: Module TMX 1.0 packages still normalize/run; TMX 1.1 declarative packages require negotiated features and never import an executable entry during install/discovery.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). TMX normalization is implemented: a 1.0 manifest normalizes to module execution without editing it (sdk.test.ts 'normalizes a 1.0 manifest to module execution'), and the declarative 1.1 path requires negotiated features (requiredFeatures is validated against KNOWN_FEATURES — an unrecognised feature is an error, not a warning). Neither install nor discovery imports an executable entry: the discovery fixture's entry THROWS on import and discovery succeeds, and the install path is extraction-only (the AT-28 sentinel test). Remaining: no real TMX 1.0 package from a previous release is installed and run end to end (the normalization is unit-tested), and the declarative packages are tested in-repo rather than installed from a packed artifact.

requirements.summary: Model/recipe/processor and protocol locks are checked for drift; updates use versioned contracts and immutable generations, preserving revocations, old choices and borrowed assets.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). Drift checking exists where the artifacts exist: the architecture gate checks the host dependency split and lock contents (check-architecture.mjs), the verification inventory records source digests so the inventory is tied to pinned text (TDD-01), and the qualification vocabulary is drift-pinned across host/SDK (the round-47 parity test). Versioned contracts and immutable generations are real: installation directories are keyed by identity AND version, the lifecycle generation advances only on successful publication, and disabled choices/revocations survive restart by persisted state. Remaining: no dedicated drift check reads the model/recipe/processor and protocol locks and fails on divergence (the requirement's named artifact set is not covered by a single gate), and 'updates preserve borrowed assets' is untested because no update flow exists.

requirements.summary: Required quality/runtime/security test skips produce a nonpassing release summary; red→green→refactor evidence and every numbered requirement have direct test links.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58). The skip-discipline is enforced at the gate level: the release gate exits nonzero while any mandatory gate is not PASS (tested by TDD-06), skips in the suite are environment-gated and reported honestly, and the verification inventory never derives PASS from the absence of failure. Direct test links: every requirement maps to an owning module, test layer and platform (TDD-01), and the traceability document maps 227 normative requirements to 90 acceptance tests. Remaining: red→green→refactor evidence is not captured as an artifact (no recorded sequence of gate transitions), and 'every numbered requirement has direct test links' is mapping-level, not link-level — the inventory names layers, not per-requirement test file paths.

requirements.summary: Run the full clean-user scenario from published/packed artifacts: prepare defaults, two modern MCP clients, direct and composed tools, custom recipe creation, lifecycle changes, cancellation and complete reproducible evidence.

evidence.evidence: Adjudicated (round 58 NOT_RUN, IMPLEMENTED round 67, EXTENDED round 70). The full clean-user scenario is an END-TO-END orchestration of almost every other acceptance item — packed install, default preparation, two modern MCP clients, direct and composed tools, recipe creation, lifecycle changes, cancellation, reproducible evidence. THE ORCHESTRATION NOW RUNS (scripts/e2e-orchestration.mjs, wired as verify:orchestration) as a 13-stage chain: packed install → listing/describe → two real lang_detect calls (de + en) → receipts show both calls → two MCP clients (authenticated 200 with a real call, unauthenticated 401) → RECIPE CREATION (round 70: the packed tool-mode-recipe CLI validates a draft, packs it into the real declarative-extension shape, and an invalid draft fails with a named refusal) → CANCELLATION (round 70: an aborted call is refused, never success, and the next call still serves) → disable withdraws the tool AND refuses the call → enable restores real inference → uninstall leaves no publication — every stage asserted, exit nonzero on any failure, stage lines printed as evidence, and the recipe-creation/cancellation stages are now REQUIRED stages so a regression fails the pipeline. Remaining: the two offline stages (title tool, hosted composition) are SKIPPED with reasons rather than run, and the run is a single-machine packed-closure chain rather than a fresh-user multi-machine matrix.
